dataset_metadata.name: Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation
dataset_metadata.institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Stanford University; Toyota Research Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Lab
dataset_metadata.citation: Severson et al. Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation. Nature Energy, vol. 4, pp. 383-391 (2019). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-019-0356-8
dataset_metadata.funding: Toyota Research Institute (Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery programme); NSF Graduate Research Fellowship DGE-114747; SAIC Innovation Center / Stanford Energy 3.0; US DOE Vehicle Technologies Office Advanced Battery Materials Research Program

cell_info.cell_notes: High-power LFP/graphite cells. Manufacturer recommended fast-charging rate: 3.6C CC-CV.

aging_modes.notes: Dataset split into three batches (2017-05-12, 2017-06-30, 2018-04-12), approximately 48 cells each. 4 cells excluded due to unexpectedly high measurement noise. Cycle lives range from ~150 to ~2,300 cycles (average 806, std 377). The dataset contains approximately 96,700 cycles total. A small diagnostic subset of cells was also cycled with periodic slow (C/10) cycles at the 1st, 100th and end-of-life cycle for degradation mode analysis (Fig. 4), but this is not a systematic RPT across all cells.

time_protocol.notes: Charging time from 0% to 80% SOC ranged from 9 to 13.3 min. Batch-specific rests: 2017-05-12 batch: 1 min rest after 80% SOC, 1 s rest after discharge; 2017-06-30 batch: 5 min rest after 80% SOC and after discharge; 2018-04-12 batch: 5 s rests after 80% SOC, after internal resistance test, and before/after discharge. Internal resistance measured at 80% SOC using 10 pulses of +/-3.6C (pulse width 30 ms for first two batches, 33 ms for third batch).

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Cell can temperature measured via Type T thermocouple attached with thermal epoxy; contact quality variable and thermocouple sometimes loses contact during cycling. CSV files exhibit occasional errors in test time and step time (resets to zero mid-cycle); these errors are corrected in the MATLAB struct files. 4C discharge curves standardized by spline fitting and interpolation to 1000 linearly spaced voltage points from 3.5 V to 2.0 V.
rawdata.known_issues: Temperature measurements not perfectly reliable for some cells (4 cells excluded from full model due to temperature probe loss of contact). 4 cells had unexpectedly high measurement noise and were excluded from analysis.

checkup.notes: No systematic periodic RPT across all cells. A diagnostic subset of cells received slow (C/10) cycles at the 1st, 100th and end-of-life cycle for degradation mode analysis only.

notes: Landmark machine-learning dataset for battery cycle life prediction. 124 commercial LFP/graphite A123 APR18650M1A cells cycled under 72 different fast-charging policies (one-step or two-step CC from 0-80% SOC, average C-rates 3.6C-6C; then 1C CC-CV to 100% SOC; uniform 4C CC-CV discharge to 2.0 V). Tests performed at 30 degrees C in forced convection environmental chamber (Amerex Instruments) on a 48-channel Arbin LBT. Data available as MATLAB structs (.mat / HDF5) and raw CSV files per cell, plus BEEP structured data. Code available at https://github.com/rdbraatz/data-driven-prediction-of-battery-cycle-life-before-capacity-degradation. Published in Nature Energy, May 2019.
